Positions.Branch/Division: Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services
Key Activities: Acquires the full range of print, non-print and electronic information resources for the Library and the department and maintains all related files.
Participates in collection development activities, including planning, information audits, product evaluation and usage reports.
Conducts system administration / problem analysis of the integrated library system; manages the Library intranet site and Library wiki.
Provides problem resolution in the integrated library system which includes adding patches, system upgrades and configuration.
Leads project teams involved in the provision of library services and products.
Trains Library staff on integrated library system functionalities.

1. DECISION MAKING: Recommends and implements changes to procedures, guidelines and other administrative and technical material for use by departmental staff or clients.
Recommends the development or modification of operational area working tools.
Resolves current issues requiring the application of procedures and precedents.
Determines the appropriate course of action when troubleshooting problems with the integrated library system.
Recommends improvements to library services to the supervisor or section head in his/her working role or as a member of a library committee and/or project team.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Assists the unit head and/or section chief in the planning and establishment of goals, priorities and training plans; and in staffing activities and employee performance reviews.
Provides guidance, coaching and orientation to co-workers and new staff and reviews the work of staff and colleagues.
Conducts training for staff and clients on standards, policies, workplace procedures and practices and the integrated library system.

Chairs and participates in working groups and project teams for special projects both internal and external to the Library. Assists in the establishment of goals, priorities and schedules; monitors and reports on progress.
3. COMMUNICATION: Responds to requests from federal government employees, clients or colleagues, using language that is easily understood, whether orally or in writing.

Requests input, information or approval of existing information from internal clients, vendors and employees in other federal government departments, using language that is clearly understood, whether orally or in writing.
Prepares reports (including financial and usage) for a range of clients both internal and external to the Library in response to requests for information.
Prepares and delivers reports to library management for analysis and decision making.
Writes information products, draft procedures, correspondence, reports, training material and memoranda for clients, colleagues and management.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of the practices, techniques and standards (e.g., Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules, 2nd edition, MAchine Readable Cataloguing) related to a specialized area within the Library in order to provide services and/or products.

Knowledge of accounting techniques and financial procedures (e.g., commitment of funds, pre‑payment, deposit accounts, group orders, discounts) to manage an acquisitions budget (e.g., track expenditures, compare estimated and actual prices, estimate budget surpluses and deficits) and to choose vendors and process orders.

Knowledge of basic UNIX, Perl scripting language, API programming and HTML coding to correct problems that occur with the integrated library system and to develop/make improvements/enhancements to the system.
Knowledge of automated library systems to evaluate, test, implement, assess system requirements, to provide input for Requests for Proposals and maintain the integrated library system.
Writing and presentation skills are required to deliver training or instruction to clients and staff.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, policies, standards, practices, procedures, integrated library system and Statistics Canada’s online catalogue to effectively deliver library services to the library’s clientele, both internal and external to the department.
Knowledge of the role, responsibilities and long term objectives of the department, its organization, programs, and regional activities to understand and fulfill information requirements.
Knowledge of departmentally supported software (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, communication, Internet) to locate, assess and disseminate information.
Knowledge of the use of databases used within the Library to create and modify records, to manipulate and extract data and to produce reports for departmental clients.

Knowledge of the acts and regulations related to the services of the Library and the department, including but not limited to the Statistics Act, Library and Archives of Canada Act, Copyright Act and Financial Administration Act to provide information to internal and external clients and to comply with audit requirements.

Knowledge of administrative principles, contract management and project management. This knowledge is required to process / manage internal transactions such as journal vouchers and contract renewals.

Knowledge of the information industry and technological trends to improve library services and reduce costs by adapting new technologies, developing new services and/or recommending changes to current practices/policies.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Investigates and resolves problems with the integrated library system (e.g., configuration changes, content management of the Online Public Access Catalogue) by analyzing system information with departmental informatics staff, contractors and vendors.
Analyzes client requests and assesses the resource options, choice of information sources and retrieval result to develop and deliver responses.
Analyzes and organizes data from the integrated library system to develop and deliver reports for library management and departmental clients.
Analyses and provides the appropriate service delivery relative to operational and client needs.
Reviews and provides feedback on the terms of contracts; participates in the selection process; and monitors progress of the work. Reports back to unit head and / or section chief.

Interprets and applies divisional policies and procedures; analyzes them in order to revise or recommend changes. These policies may or may not be clearly defined, but contribute to the audit function and/or affect the delivery of service and access to information of departmental employees, other government employees and the general public.
